query: Which published studies, national inventories, and external audit protocols are best for validating field methods and replicating results on a subset of e-waste sites?

response.query: Which published studies, national inventories, and external audit protocols are best for validating field methods and replicating results on a subset of e-waste sites?
response.answer: The best studies for validating field methods on e-waste sites are the National E-waste Assessment Report for Trinidad and Tobago and the U.S. EPA Criteria for Product Category Rules. These documents provide robust frameworks and guidelines.

results.title: Appendix M to Part 51, Title 40
results.content: For pollutants that exist in the gas phase at ambient temperature, the audit sample shall consist of an appropriate concentration of the pollutant in air or nitrogen that will be introduced into the sampling system of the test method at or near the same entry point as a sample from the emission source. This procedure calls for using an FIA in conjunction with various configurations of impingers, and other absorbents, or adsorbents to determine the best EPA Method 18 sampling train configuration for the assessment and capture of VOCs. VOC compounds present in the exhaust gas from processes located at CWM facilities fall into five general categories: Alcohols, aldehydes, acetate esters, ketones, and carboxylic acids, and typically contain fewer than six carbon atoms. For calibration gas values not generally available (*i.e.*, organics between 1 and 10 percent by volume), alternative methods for preparing calibration gas mixtures, such as dilution systems (Test Method 205, 40 CFR Part 51, Appendix M), may be used with prior approval of the Administrator.
